oneTimers: Investment gains of $1,876M before tax ($1,480M after tax) were mostly locked in, not paper: after-tax realized gains on sales were $11.2B in the quarter — taxable gains were $14.2B before tax on about $20.0B of stock sales, mainly trimming Apple — partly offset by a $9.7B after-tax fall in unrealized gains, much of it those same Apple gains leaving the unsold pile. The unrealized part can just as easily reverse next quarter.

No significant catastrophe events hit in the first quarter of 2024, while a year ago a cyclone and floods in New Zealand cost about $350M after tax. GEICO's pre-tax underwriting earnings jumped to $1,928M from $703M as its loss ratio fell to 72.5% from 83.0%.
Currency moves on foreign debt: revaluing Berkshire's non-dollar borrowings produced a gain of about $597M after tax inside the 'Other' operating earnings line, versus a $17M loss a year ago.

Berkshire bought the remaining 20% of Pilot Travel Centers in January 2024 for $2.6B, taking its ownership to 100% — Pilot, the truck-stop chain, contributed $12.5B of revenue in the quarter on the segment basis.
otherDetail: Investment gains of $1,876M — mostly gains on Berkshire's stock portfolio — plus $493M of equity-method earnings, less $130M attributable to noncontrolling interests.

takeaways.text: The businesses themselves earned $11.2B after tax, up from $8.1B a year ago — insurance underwriting nearly tripled to $2.6B as GEICO's loss ratio fell 10.5 points to 72.5%, and insurance investment income rose to $2.6B as Treasury Bill yields lifted interest income.
takeaways.title: Operating earnings rose 39%

takeaways.text: Headline profit was $12.7B, down from $35.5B a year ago even though the businesses improved — investment gains were $1.9B before tax, versus $34.8B a year ago. Berkshire sold about $20B of stocks in the quarter, mostly Apple: Apple was worth $135.4B at March 31, down from $174.3B at year-end.
takeaways.title: Headline profit fell — the year-ago bar was the stock market

takeaways.text: Cash, equivalents and Treasury Bills reached about $189B at March 31 — Berkshire received $20.0B from stock sales in the quarter and spent only $2.7B buying, parking the money in Treasury Bills. Insurance float was about $168B.
takeaways.title: The cash pile set a record

verdict: Berkshire's operating earnings rose 39% to $11.2B as insurance underwriting nearly tripled to $2.6B on GEICO's recovery, while headline profit fell to $12.7B from $35.5B a year ago because investment gains shrank to $1.9B from $34.8B.
